EICMA 2026 • Yamaha Births New Adventure Scooter Family, Three RW Models That Look More Like Motorcycles
New VW ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Is All About the Present and Future of the Brand's Supermini Hot Hatch
10 photos
Photo: Volkswagen
There have been several important premieres this week, and while some of them were celebrated at the 2026 Los Angeles Auto Show , others were simply unveiled over the World Wide Web, as that’s a lot cheaper, not to mention that the reach is pretty much the same.
One of them was the Lamborghini Temerario Spyder, the brand’s first-ever supercar to feature a power-folding hardtop, and to be honest, it did not get much traction in our news feed. Hyundai has a new Elantra in its lineup, Honda presented an updated version of its Civic Type R, alongside the Type R HRC Concept, and there is a new Honda Avancier, too, among a whole bunch of other things.
Mind you, the Temerario Spyder wasn’t the only big premiere of the week that enthusiasts do not seem to care about that much, as the same goes for one particular Volkswagen. It’s none other than the ID. Polo GTI Clubsport, and unlike its non-Clubsport sibling, you cannot buy this one. Well, not yet anyway, because it is nothing more than a mere concept at this point, though it could preview an upcoming Clubsport version of the brand’s supermini electric hot hatch.
That’s what the rumor mill says anyway, and to be honest, we wouldn’t be surprised if Volkswagen decided to keep it as a concept. After all, it wouldn’t be the only GTI study that did not offer a glimpse of something more special. You do remember the W12-650 from almost two decades ago, and the GTI Roadster Vision Gran Turismo from 2014, don’t you? None of them made it to production, by the way.
Photo: Volkswagen This two-door concept looks a lot more aggressive than the regular Volkswagen ID. Polo GTI . The Clubsport has two fewer doors, features a vented hood, a big spoiler at the rear, fat wheel arches, and a few other special changes. The livery is also exclusive to the concept, alongside the retro-inspired alloys, and so on. And for what it’s worth, it kind of looks like something that would feel at home in the WRC world, which is a compliment, by the way.
The changes continue on the inside, where it features Recarco bucket seats and five-pointed harnesses, as well as a real roll cage. There are no back seats anymore, and ArtVelours microfleece fabric can be seen in the cabin. The tablet infotainment screen is still a thing, because apparently VW couldn’t make do without it.
Based on the same MEB+ platform as its production sibling, the VW ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept features an electric motor that drives the front wheels, just like the regular ID. Polo GTI. However, the motor powering the study was sourced from the RWD ID.3 Neo GTI and the ID.7, so it brings a heck of a lot more power. Like 63% more. The output is now rated at 362 hp (270 kW/367 ps) as opposed to 222 hp (166 kW/226 ps) on the production model.
During the short acceleration bursts, the show car is said to unleash 389 hp (290 kW/394 ps), allowing this one-off VW GTI to hit 62 mph (100 kph) in 4.7 seconds, or 2.1 seconds faster than the ID. Polo GTI. The top speed is 155 mph (250 kph). And let’s not forget than no ICE-powered GTI drops below the 5-second zone, as the only one that does is the AWD Golf R, which has 329 hp (245 kW/333 ps) to play with.
Photo: Volkswagen Volkswagen’s new ID. Polo GTI Clubsport Concept is the latest model in a string of cars that is all about the brand’s GTI celebrations, as 2026 marks the 50th anniversary of the original Golf GTI . Between us, it definitely looks like something that the automaker could easily put into production as a more upscale version of the EV-powered supermini hot hatch.
If it does indeed hit the assembly line, then chances are it will have a five-door body, and it likely won’t look as aggressive as the study. The bucket seats, harnesses, and roll cage should also be scrapped, and the back seat reintroduced. On top of these, we wouldn’t be surprised if it did not use the punchier electric motor, though that’s pure assumption at this point.
In conclusion, as we previously mentioned, there is no word on whether Volkswagen indeed plans to launch a Clubsport version of the ID. Polo GTI or not, so we cannot tell you if such a thing will get the green light for production. It would indeed be an interesting addition to the brand’s GTI family, and just like the regular hot hatch, it would be kept away from our shores, so the only way to admire it in America would be from the World Wide Web.
Should VW launch an ID. Polo GTI Clubsport in your opinion? And if so, should they bring it to our market, too? Tell us all about it in the comments area below.
